note_sections.t: Clinical attention sought due to a previous prostate cancer diagnosis coupled with a recent serum PSA rise to 4.8 ng/mL.

At sixty-seven years of age, this widowed patient has a documented history of a prior positive biopsy confirming low-grade malignancy. Initial evaluation for an elevated PSA occurred in 2022. He experiences moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, scoring 16 on the IPSS questionnaire, dominated by nocturia and a diminished urinary stream that have not progressed recently. Occupational background includes work as a retired mechanical engineer. He resides independently. Lifestyle factors include being a Non-smoker, consuming six alcoholic units weekly, and participating in weekly swimming sessions. Past medical encounters involve standard audiology and vascular surgery visits for unrelated aging processes, with no other significant comorbidities or active medications reported. He explicitly denies bone discomfort, haematuria, or constitutional complaints.

Normal DRE: Symmetrically enlarged gland exhibiting a uniform, smooth consistency without focal hardening or asymmetry. Systemic inspection shows stable hemodynamic parameters, clear lung fields, and absence of peripheral edema or palpable lymph nodes.
